# google_compute_dhcp_options_config

A standalone, regional Compute Engine resource that encapsulates a set of
user-defined DHCP configurations for custom NTP, domain search, lease time,
and iPXE/TFTP network boot options.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](../guides/provider_versions.html.markdown) for more details on beta resources.

To get more information about DhcpOptionsConfig, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/beta/dhcpOptionsConfigs)
* How-to Guides
    * [VPC network overview](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc)

## Example Usage - Compute Dhcp Options Config Basic


```hcl
resource "google_compute_dhcp_options_config" "default" {
  provider = google-beta

  name   = "my-dhcp-config"
  region = "us-central1"
}
```

## Example Usage - Compute Dhcp Options Config Full


```hcl
resource "google_compute_network" "net1" {
  provider = google-beta

  name                    = "my-dhcp-net-1"
  auto_create_subnetworks = false
}

resource "google_compute_dhcp_options_config" "default" {
  provider = google-beta

  name        = "my-dhcp-config"
  region      = "us-central1"
  description = "Initial DHCP options configuration"

  lease_time_sec             = 3600
  domain_name                = "corp.example.com"
  dns_search_paths           = ["corp.example.com", "svc.example.com"]
  ntp_server_ipv4_addresses  = ["192.0.2.10", "192.0.2.11"]
  ntp_server_ipv6_addresses  = ["2001:db8::10", "2001:db8::11"]
  tftp_server_ipv4_name      = "tftp.corp.example.com"
  tftp_server_ipv4_addresses = ["192.0.2.20", "192.0.2.21"]
  boot_file_ipv4_name        = "pxelinux.0"
  boot_file_ipv6_url         = "tftp://[2001:db8::20]/bootx64.efi"
  boot_file_ipv6_parameters  = ["console=ttyS0", "quiet"]

  associations {
    name    = "assoc-1"
    network = google_compute_network.net1.id
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `name` -
  (Required)
  Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is created.
  The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with RFC1035.
  Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match the regular
  expression `[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?` which means the first character
  must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must be a dash,
  lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which cannot be a dash.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  An optional description of this resource.

* `lease_time_sec` -
  (Optional)
  The duration, in seconds, of the IPv4 address lease offered by the DHCP
  server to the client VM guest OS (between 3600 and 4294967295).
  Corresponds to DHCPv4 Option 51.

* `domain_name` -
  (Optional)
  The domain name that the client VM guest OS should use when resolving
  hostnames via DNS (e.g., `example.com`). It defines the default domain
  suffix for the client. Corresponds to DHCPv4 Option 15.

* `dns_search_paths` -
  (Optional)
  An ordered list of domain suffixes (search paths) that the client VM guest
  OS should append to resolve hostnames that are not fully qualified.
  Applies to both DHCPv4 Option 119 and DHCPv6 Option 24.

* `ntp_server_ipv4_addresses` -
  (Optional)
  An ordered list of IPv4 addresses of Network Time Protocol (NTP) servers
  available to the client VM guest OS for system clock synchronization,
  listed in order of preference. Corresponds to DHCPv4 Option 42.

* `ntp_server_ipv6_addresses` -
  (Optional)
  An ordered list of IPv6 addresses of Network Time Protocol (NTP) servers
  available to the client VM guest OS for system clock synchronization.
  Corresponds to DHCPv6 Option 56.

* `tftp_server_ipv4_name` -
  (Optional)
  The hostname or IP address of the Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP)
  server from which the client VM guest OS can download boot files.
  Corresponds to DHCPv4 Option 66.

* `tftp_server_ipv4_addresses` -
  (Optional)
  An ordered list of one or more IPv4 addresses of TFTP servers.
  Corresponds to DHCPv4 Option 150.

* `boot_file_ipv4_name` -
  (Optional)
  The file path and name of the boot image/file on the TFTP server that the
  client VM guest OS should download and execute during network boot.
  Corresponds to DHCPv4 Option 67.

* `boot_file_ipv6_url` -
  (Optional)
  The Uniform Resource Locator (URL) specifying the protocol, server address,
  and file path of the boot file that the client VM guest OS should download
  and execute for network boot (e.g., `tftp://[2001:db8::1]/bootx64.efi` or
  `http://[2001:db8::1]/boot.img`). Corresponds to DHCPv6 Option 59.

* `boot_file_ipv6_parameters` -
  (Optional)
  A list of UTF-8 encoded parameter strings to be passed as arguments to the
  bootloader program or OS kernel after downloading the boot file.
  Corresponds to DHCPv6 Option 60.

* `associations` -
  (Optional)
  Mapping of user-defined keys to Network associations for this DHCP options
  configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_associations).

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The region where the DHCP options config resides.
  If it is not provided, the provider region is used.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) The deletion policy for the DHCP options configuration.
Setting `deletion_policy = "FORCE"` clears any remaining network `associations`
before deleting the configuration. By default (`DEFAULT`), Terraform attempts to
delete the resource directly, which fails if any `associations` still exist on
the resource.

When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", the command will behave as if set to "DEFAULT".

Possible values: `DEFAULT`, `FORCE`, `PREVENT`, `ABANDON`, `DELETE`.



<a name="nested_associations"></a>The `associations` block supports:

* `name` - (Required) The identifier for this object. Format specified above.

* `network` -
  (Required)
  The target VPC network this DHCP options configuration is attached to,
  specified as a full or partial URL or network name in the same project.

* `network_id` -
  (Output)
  The server-defined ID of the associated Network.

* `state` -
  (Output)
  State of the association (for example, `ACTIVE` or `ORPHANED`).

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/dhcpOptionsConfigs/{{name}}`

* `dhcp_options_config_id` -
  The unique identifier for the resource. This identifier is defined by the server.

* `creation_timestamp` -
  Creation timestamp in RFC3339 text format.
* `self_link` - The URI of the created resource.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


DhcpOptionsConfig can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/dhcpOptionsConfigs/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import DhcpOptionsConfig using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-required value->"
    region = "<-optional value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_compute_dhcp_options_config.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import DhcpOptionsConfig using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/dhcpOptionsConfigs/{{name}}"
  to = google_compute_dhcp_options_config.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), DhcpOptionsConfig can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_compute_dhcp_options_config.default projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/dhcpOptionsConfigs/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_compute_dhcp_options_config.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_compute_dhcp_options_config.default {{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_compute_dhcp_options_config.default {{name}}
```
